overview.title: Classroom Overview
overview.body:
The flexible design decouples ventilation air and loads, allowing the DOAS units to handle latent loads and condition air while secondary HVAC systems handle sensible loads. This approach provides better control, energy efficiency, and comfort. Proper control is essential for maintaining comfort and extending equipment lifespan.

Featured Equipment

  • Dedicated Outdoor Air System (DOAS) with energy recovery
  • Secondary HVAC system (not provided by Greenheck)

systemEquipment.title: RVE-85
systemEquipment.body:
• Direct drive plenum supply and optional exhaust fans with neoprene isolation and factory-provided variable frequency drive.
  • 2-inch double-wall cabinet with R13 injected foam insulation. R13 foam insulation thermally broken. Exterior Finish Permatector™ (2,500 hr salt spray rating under ASTM B117 testing conditions)

systemEquipment.title: ATU - XG-TH-500
systemEquipment.body:
• Damper rotates in a self-lubricating, long-life, low-friction thermoplastic bearing
  • Industry leading continuous welded primary inlet duct to minimize leakage with three stiffening beads for added rigidity
  • Mechanically fastened damper assembly shall be double layer, 18-gauge equivalent, galvanized

designNarrative.title: Classroom Design Narrative
designNarrative.body:
The Dedicated Outdoor Air System (DOAS) model handles latent loads and conditions air while secondary HVAC systems handle sensible loads. The design centers on a Greenheck model RVE-85, rooftop ventilator equipped with a polymer total energy recovery wheel and a packaged Air Source Heat Pump (ASHP) with electric secondary heating.

The unit includes modulating, inverter scroll compressors, electronically commutated (EC) on all condenser fan motors, and modulating hot gas reheat. Supply and exhaust fans are controlled by factory provided, field mounted duct static pressure sensors.

Each room features motorized, single duct VAV boxes, Greenheck model XG-TH-500, which open/close based on occupancy to maintain ventilation. Air terminal units have 1" fiberglass insulation with 1 1/2 lb weight and connect to a Greenheck XG-5750 air diffuser.

overview.title: Gym Overview
overview.body:
The gymnasium features a single-zone, variable airflow system designed for high occupancy and activity levels. The system includes demand-controlled ventilation and high-volume, low-speed fans for optimal air circulation.

Featured Equipment

  • High Volume Low Speed (HVLS) fans
  • Demand-controlled ventilation system

systemEquipment.title: HVLS Fan
systemEquipment.body:
• High-volume, low-speed fan for large open spaces.
  • Improves air circulation and comfort.

systemEquipment.title: RV-110
systemEquipment.body:
• Rooftop ventilation unit optimized for large spaces.
  • Energy-efficient operation with advanced controls.

designNarrative.title: Gym Design Narrative
designNarrative.body: The gymnasium features a single-zone, variable airflow system designed for high occupancy and activity levels. The design centers on a Greenheck model RV-110 rooftop unit for ventilation, supplemented by high-volume, low-speed (HVLS) fans to ensure optimal air circulation and occupant comfort.

systemEquipment.title: VAV Box
systemEquipment.body:
• Precision airflow control for individual zones.
  • Quiet operation suitable for office environments.

systemEquipment.title: Air Diffuser
systemEquipment.body:
• Ensures proper air distribution within the office space.
  • Aesthetically designed to blend with ceiling grids.

designNarrative.title: Admin Offices Design Narrative
designNarrative.body: Administrative areas utilize a Multi-zone Variable Air Volume (VAV) system. This setup allows for individual temperature control in different offices using Greenheck VAV boxes and air diffusers, ensuring comfort while maximizing energy efficiency.

systemEquipment.title: Make-Up Air
systemEquipment.body:
• Replaces exhausted air to maintain pressure balance.
  • Tempered air for occupant comfort.

systemEquipment.title: Exhaust Fan
systemEquipment.body:
• Removes stale air and odors.
  • High efficiency and low sound levels.

designNarrative.title: Cafeteria Design Narrative
designNarrative.body: The cafeteria ventilation system is designed to handle variable occupancy loads and food odors. It integrates Greenheck make-up air units with the kitchen's exhaust system to maintain pressure balance and prevent odor migration into adjacent spaces.

systemEquipment.title: Vari-Flow Hood
systemEquipment.body:
• High-efficiency grease extraction and containment.
  • Integrated LED lighting and fire suppression.

systemEquipment.title: Pollution Control
systemEquipment.body:
• Removes grease and odors from exhaust air.
  • Ensures compliance with environmental regulations.

designNarrative.title: Kitchen Design Narrative
designNarrative.body: The kitchen requires a robust ventilation system to capture heat, grease, and odors. A dedicated Greenheck Make-Up Air Unit pairs with Vari-Flow Exhaust Hoods and a Pollution Control Unit to ensure safety, compliance, and comfort for kitchen staff.

systemEquipment.title: Air Curtain
systemEquipment.body:
• Creates an air seal to prevent infiltration.
  • Keeps conditioned air inside and pests outside.

systemEquipment.title: DOAS Unit
systemEquipment.body:
• Supplies conditioned outdoor air.
  • Maintains optimal indoor air quality.

designNarrative.title: Lobby Design Narrative
designNarrative.body: The lobby serves as a transition space, requiring a system that can handle rapid load changes. Greenheck Air Curtains protect against infiltration at the entry, while a dedicated DOAS unit maintains a comfortable, conditioned environment for occupants.

systemEquipment.title: Energy Recovery
systemEquipment.body:
• Transfers heat and moisture between airstreams.
  • Reduces heating and cooling loads.

designNarrative.title: Locker Room Design Narrative
designNarrative.body: Locker rooms require high ventilation rates to effectively control humidity and odors. A Greenheck Energy Recovery Ventilator (ERV) provides ample fresh air while recovering energy from the exhaust stream to minimize operating costs.

systemEquipment.title: Fume Exhaust
systemEquipment.body:
• High-velocity discharge to safely disperse fumes.
  • Corrosion-resistant construction.

systemEquipment.title: Venturi Valve
systemEquipment.body:
• Maintains precise airflow and room pressurization.
  • Fast response to changing conditions.

designNarrative.title: Science Lab Design Narrative
designNarrative.body: Safety is paramount in science labs. The ventilation system uses Greenheck high-plume exhaust fans to safely disperse fumes and Venturi valves to maintain precise room pressurization and containment of hazardous substances.
